title: Frontier Town
paragraphs: Western adventure about lawyer Chad Remington, who returns to the frontier town of Dos Rios and becomes a crime-fighting attorney in a community caught between the old West and a new legal order.

Syndicated Western legal-adventure series built around Chad Remington and Cherokee O’Bannon in Dos Rios. The 48-object GRH container represents 47 underlying numbered stories plus one exact duplicate archive copy of program #2.
The run breaks into several distinct periods: Original documented syndication schedule (March 5, 1949 to January 21, 1950) and Later GRH syndication schedule (September 26, 1952 to August 14, 1953).

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Bruce Eells (producer), Paul Franklin (director and writer), Wade Crosby (performer), Bill Forman (announcer), Ivan Ditmars (organist, composer, and conductor), [[person|reed-hadley|Reed Hadley]] (performer), and [[person|jeff-chandler|Jeff Chandler]] (performer).

The stories often return to western frontier community, law, courts and frontier justice, outlaws, robbery and violent crime, land, homesteading and property conflict, cattle, ranching and trail drives, and railroads, stages and transport.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Transcription syndication and local commercial insertion, Multiple market/distribution chronologies, and Frontier law and legal-order storytelling.
